producer_report.summary: Reopened in the firstmate study is now a waiting state with a move back to Queued, and only Done "ends the task". Root cause: model.json marked `reopened` as terminal-success, and the intro and glossary repeated that. I added a Reopened→Queued transition (t12) because the model's dead-end rule needs a waiting state to have a way out, and I wrote its summary in intro.json. I also changed xtask/src/site.rs, which the brief did not list. One test asserted the wrong "ends the task" tag on Reopened, and two tests counted transitions or cards. All 154 tests in `cargo test -p xtask` pass, including the site_page and policy tests. I did not run clippy, fmt or the full workspace test. The Queued return is not cited by any existing claim; I did not add one (see open_issues).

checks_run.note: Passed on the second rerun. The first run failed on t12's missing summary. The second failed on a test that asserted the old Reopened tag and on two count assertions, all now updated. The run includes tests/policy.rs, the boundary scan.

criteria_check.criterion: In studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json the 'reopened' state no longer has kind 'terminal-success'; it is a non-terminal kind (e.g. waiting), or the item returns to 'queued', consistent with bin/fm-teardown.sh sending the backlog row back to Queued.
criteria_check.evidence: model.json: reopened kind is now "waiting"; new transition t12 goes from reopened to queued. `cargo test -p xtask` passes, including the test that checks the rendered page tags reopened as waiting.

criteria_check.criterion: studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json 'states' lead-in no longer says Done and Reopened both carry 'ends the task'. It says only Done ends the task, and that Reopened sends the item back to Queued for the captain's answer. Grep for 'ends the task' confirms.
criteria_check.evidence: The lead-in now reads: Only Done carries the tag "ends the task". Reopened does not end the task: the backlog row goes back to Queued for the captain's answer. The updated test asserts "Only Done carries the tag" is on the page and "Done and Reopened both carry" is not.

criteria_check.criterion: The 'reopened' glossary definition in intro.json, and any transition out of Reopened added to model.json, match the cited claims c23-c25 and the Queued return, with no new uncited claims.
criteria_check.evidence: The glossary entry and t12 both cite only c23, c24 and c25. I added no new claim. The tests that fail on an uncited intro element pass. The Queued return itself has no citation of its own in claims.json; see open_issues.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test (the study/record validation tests over studies/) and cargo clippy: they pass with the edited study files. The source check on the study page for the reopened state passes, as shown in the recorded check output.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks for clippy and the full test. I ran `cargo test --locked -p xtask`: 154 tests pass across the unit, ci_shards, fingerprint, policy, site_page, spec and walltime targets.

open_issues: The Queued return is cited only through c23-c25, which describe the reopen and say nothing of Queued. If the check needs a claim that quotes fm-teardown.sh around lines 3894-3896, someone with the pinned source should add it. I had no access to the source or its pinned checkout.

claims.json and validation.json are unchanged. I could not verify a Queued source quote, so I added no claim. The validation rules in validation.json were already all passing and nothing I changed affects them.
mistakes: I first edited only the study files and the cargo test failed. I had not checked the xtask tests that encode the study's shape, and that cost two rerun cycles.
learnings: The study validator's dead-end rule requires every non-terminal state to have an outgoing transition, and the site renderer requires a summary in intro.json for every transition.
xtask/src/site.rs holds tests that hardcode the study's transition count (12) and its count of "No guard applies" cards (4).
The `grep` command is not allowed in Bash for this role; use the Grep tool.
desires: Read access to the pinned firstmate source, to cite the Queued return in a new claim.
